corrected_value.title: Feeling Superior Is a Bipartisan Issue

decisions.quote:
Toner, Leary, Asher, and Jongman-Sereno (2013) found that dogmatism
                                was higher among conservatives than liberals, but both conservatives and liberals with extreme attitudes reported higher
                                perceived superiority of beliefs. In the current study, we conducted a preregistered direct and conceptual replication
                                of this previous research using a large nationally representative sample.
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly identifies Toner, Leary, Asher, and Jongman-Sereno (2013; 'Feeling superior is a bipartisan issue: Extremity (not direction) of political views predicts perceived belief superiority', Psychological Science, DOI: 10.1177/0956797613494848) as the single published study whose findings it directly and conceptually replicates. Shipped row 969 and blind target 0 identify the same original study.

decisions.quote:
Consistent with Toner et al.’s findings, our
                                results showed that conservatives had higher dogmatism scores than liberals, whereas both conservative and liberal
                                extreme attitudes were associated with higher belief superiority compared with more moderate attitudes. As in their
                                study, we also found that whether conservative or liberal attitudes were associated with higher belief superiority was
                                topic dependent. Contrasting Toner et al.’s findings, our results also showed that ideologically extreme individuals had
                                higher dogmatism.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind code 'mixed'. The authors confirm Toner et al.'s (2013) findings regarding higher average dogmatism among conservatives (linear effect), higher belief superiority among both conservative and liberal extremists (quadratic effect with a linear effect statistically equivalent to zero), and topic dependence of belief superiority, but explicitly contrast their significant quadratic (curvilinear) relationship between ideological extremity and dogmatism with Toner et al.'s null quadratic dogmatism finding (which the preregistered analysis plan required to be smaller than the smallest effect size of interest for a full replication of the dogmatism finding). Under the codebook, confirming some tested relationships while explicitly contrasting another yields 'mixed'.

decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind code 'replication'. The authors collected new survey data from a nationally representative Lucid sample (N = 1,319; n = 707 after attention-check exclusions) to directly and conceptually re-test the published findings of Toner et al. (2013).
